summary.text: A crystal is a solid whose atoms, molecules or ions are arranged in a highly ordered structure, a lattice that extends in all directions.
Most inorganic solids are not single crystals but polycrystals, many microscopic crystals fused into one solid, including most metals, rocks, ceramics and ice.
What makes something a crystal is its microscopic atomic arrangement, not its shape, though flat faces with sharp angles are common.

facts.label: Word origin
facts.value: From Ancient Greek krustallos, meaning both ice and rock crystal

facts.label: Lead crystal
facts.value: Not a crystal at all, but a type of glass

facts.label: Where most are
facts.value: Largest concentrations by volume are in Earth's solid bedrock

items.prompt: A shop sells wine glasses labelled lead crystal. Scientifically, what is wrong with the name?

options.label: The material is too soft to hold the repeating pattern a crystal needs
The material is a single crystal, which is not what the label claims
The material is glass, which has no periodic atomic structure
The material is a crystal, but one far too small to see

items.explain: Lead crystal and crystal glass are types of glass, which are amorphous solids, not crystals.

items.prompt: A geologist holds a rough grain with no flat faces at all. Could it still be a crystal?

options.label: Yes, because a crystal is defined by its atomic arrangement, not its outer shape
No, because a crystal must always have flat faces
No, because rough surfaces mean the atoms are random
Yes, but only if it is table salt

items.explain: A crystal is defined by its microscopic atomic arrangement, not its macroscopic shape. Anhedral crystals lack well-formed faces, usually because they are one grain in a polycrystalline solid.

items.prompt: A copper pipe looks like one uniform piece of metal. What would you find inside at a microscopic scale?

options.label: One giant crystal running the full length
Atoms scattered in no pattern at all
A smooth liquid film around each atom
Many tiny crystals fused together

items.explain: Most metals are polycrystals, made of many microscopic crystals fused into a single solid.

items.prompt: A lab watches two melts cool and harden, one into a crystal and one into a glass. Which one gives off latent heat of fusion as it forms?

options.label: The one that forms a glass
The one that forms a crystal
Both do, in equal amounts
Neither does, since both are cooling down

items.explain: Forming a glass does not release the latent heat of fusion, but forming a crystal does.

items.prompt: A crystal grows in a solution. Where do new atoms attach most easily, and what shape results?

options.label: To the flat faces, so the crystal grows rougher over time
Evenly everywhere, so the crystal grows into a ball
To rough, unstable parts of the surface, so the flat stable faces grow larger and smoother
Only to the corners, so the crystal grows long spikes

items.explain: New atoms attach easily to rougher, less stable parts but less easily to flat, stable surfaces, so the flat surfaces tend to grow larger and smoother.

items.prompt: Two crystals of the same mineral form in different surroundings and end up with different outer shapes. What explains this?

options.label: The conditions where each one grew also shape its visible form
The inner structure of each one must be completely different
One of them must really be a glass
Only the crystal's chemistry can affect its shape

items.explain: A crystal's habit is determined by its crystal structure, its chemistry and bonding, and the conditions under which it formed.
